title: Require destructive approval for GitHub sync mutations
goal: Ensure terminal sync operations that can delete local or remote workspace files require the destructive capability and are denied when approval is required.
context: CommandRegistry currently classifies `sync now` as network+write, but GitHubRepositorySyncClient can propagate local and remote deletions during synchronization. UserConfiguredPolicyEvaluator treats destructive capability as approval-required, so omitting `.destructive` bypasses that safeguard.
forbidden_changes: Do not weaken UserConfiguredPolicyEvaluator or grant destructive actions by default.
Do not change sync conflict/rollback semantics or token handling.
Do not mark preview as a destructive mutation.
acceptance_criteria: The `sync now` command requires network, write, and destructive capabilities.
A regression test proves the authorizer sees destructive and denies execution before the handler runs.
Sync preview remains read-only and does not require destructive capability.
verification: Check Swift package tests + repository integrity and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA.
recovery: Revert the single task commit if preview permissions change or sync mutations bypass destructive authorization.
